items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: The interviewee only responds 'To get paid' to the interviewer's statement about Mousy Alexander replacing Morey Feld; no personal interaction or relationship is described.

ctx.x: I did. It was, you know you had some bizarre moments with him, but you know that was like playing with one of my childhood heroes. He was a giant. And some of the players, you know it was like major league baseball. So I thought it was wonderful. And every once in a while something strange would happen, but the plusses outweighed the minuses.

I think you were safer with Benny in a big band. The more people around, he couldn’t, it was harder to single somebody out. But in Las Vegas, he didn’t like the drummer. who’d been playing with him for years, Morey Feld, who is a perfectly good drummer. And he sent for Mousy Alexander from New York to come all the way to Las Vegas for the last, well, three weeks altogether, Mousy came and played the last two weeks and Morey Feld had to sit there in a tuxedo every night.
